title: The Hiding Place in the Cliff

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: An elder climbs to the children's cliff fort and knows it was once a hiding place: tell the children, or just let them play.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: High in the cliffs there's a narrow cave with a hidden entrance, and inside, old stone walls and a ledge for sleeping. The children have discovered it and made it their fort. (subject), an elder, has climbed up to see. (subject.He/she) knows what it was: a place where people hid, a very long time ago, when there was danger from the sea.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) sits down on the old ledge. (subject.He/she) tells the children, gently, that a long time ago, people hid here when they were frightened, and stayed safe. (friend) looks around the little cave with different eyes. "Should we leave?" (subject) shakes (subject.his/her) head. "I think they'd be glad it's a fort now. Somewhere children play instead of hide." The children keep the fort. They're quieter in it than before.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) doesn't say anything. (subject.He/she) sits on the ledge and watches the children play seals and turtles and storms. It's strange, and a little sad, and also good, to hear laughing in a place that once held people holding their breath. When (subject.he/she) climbs down, (subject.he/she) leaves a little stack of flat stones by the entrance, the way you might for someone you remember.
